narrative.overview: The agreed direction is calm, elegant, and minimalistic. Clear hierarchy, precise alignment, consistent spacing, and purposeful visuals support understanding. The existing template defines the visual identity; this document is the visual specification for Slidev and Impeccable.

rules.name: Opening title slide
rules.body: The opening Title slide displays the full episode title, season number, and episode number. Use the Title layout below, with the episode title as the main heading and the season and episode identifiers in the subtitle. For the unnumbered Prologue, show its title without inventing season or episode numbers.

rules.name: Slide numbering
rules.body:
Show a plain `n/m` counter in the lower-right corner on every slide, including Title and Section slides. Count the initial state and each successive click/build stage as one numbered slide; `m` is the total of these states across the deck. Advance or reverse `n` with navigation, keeping `m` fixed. Continuous animation frames do not count separately. These display numbers do not change the authored slide count or outline in the teacher notes.

Use the secondary typography role (38 px, light, neutral gray), right edge x ≈ 1863 and bottom edge y ≈ 1060. Keep the counter clear of teaching content and logos, without a surrounding box or decoration.

rules.name: Diagram connectors
rules.body:
- Stop connector strokes and arrowheads just short of object outlines, leaving a small, visible gap at both ends. Keep their entire paths clear of objects and labels.
- An arrow intended as an arch uses one smooth curve, without an appended straight segment or kink. Intentional elbow connectors remain appropriate where the diagram calls for them.
- Align arrowheads with the path's endpoint direction. Keep anchors and clearances consistent when a connection reverses direction or changes state.

rules.name: Build-stage consistency
rules.body: Each build stage must show a coherent state of the explanation. When an object appears, include the contents it already has at that point; show an empty object only when the approved process requires it, such as a computer before cloning. Reveal subsequent changes at their intended steps, preserving existing contents until the process changes them.

rules.name: Markdown authoring and rendering
rules.body:
The Prologue renderer implements this contract. Slide content is authored in Markdown; the renderer supplies the HTML structure. Other existing decks are not migrated automatically. `General content two column` is an explicit two-column variant of `General content`. The author selects it through `slideType` and writes ordinary Markdown. The renderer owns the containers and styling; author-written HTML wrappers or CSS classes such as `body`, `spacious`, `sparse`, `columns`, and `coverage` are not required. Both columns have consistent, equal widths and a fixed gap, with left-aligned text and natural line wrapping within each column. The title spans both columns and follows the General content title treatment. Column placement, typography, and spacing are shared layout rules rather than slide-specific adjustments. #### Automatic distribution Without an explicit break, the renderer decides where the left column ends and the right column begins. It preserves source order: read down the left column, then down the right column. Balance uses rendered content height, including wrapped lines and spacing, rather than simply counting bullets. Keep each list item, its nested content, and other logical content blocks together. Nested lists express hierarchy; an ordinary paragraph is ordinary column content, not a special introductory region. For five bullets of comparable height, prefer three on the left and two on the right. ```md --- slideType: General content two column --- # What Are Projects? - Collaborative enterprise - Carefully planned - Temporary rather than permanent - Accomplish particular tasks - Time constraints ``` #### Explicit column break An author can override automatic distribution with one `::columnBreak::` marker on its own line, separated from surrounding content by blank lines. Body content before the marker goes in the left column; body content after it goes in the right column. The heading remains above both columns. The renderer honors this boundary rather than moving items across it to improve balance. The marker itself is not displayed. ```md --- slideType: General content two column --- # What Are Projects? - Collaborative enterprise - Carefully planned - Temporary rather than permanent ::columnBreak:: - Accomplish particular tasks - Time constraints ``` This is course-specific behavior implemented through Slidev’s named-slot syntax. The same renderer and column styling handle both modes. Automatic and explicit distribution use the same column geometry and typography. Neither mode may shrink text below the design minimum, reorder content, add columns, or create slides to make overflowing content fit. Overflow must be reported for review. #### Shared content rules - Write headings, paragraphs, lists, nested lists, and images in Markdown. No `lead` class, layout wrappers, manual `
` tags, or author-written Vue component tags are needed. - Content begins at y ≈ 355, or below a wrapping title with a 48 px gap, and has a lower boundary at y = 950. Keep both columns aligned at the top and left-aligned within their fixed widths. - Top-level body text starts at 64 px; nested bullets use 52 px. If the measured composition does not fit, the renderer uses the permitted 52 px body size for both columns and measures again. It never shrinks below 52 px or changes slide count. - Use a consistent 32 px gap between top-level content units and 20 px within nested groups. Do not vertically stretch sparse content to fill the region. - The same semantics apply to single-column content. Parent bullets stay with their nested bullets; paragraphs take part in normal flow. There is no special full-width introduction or `lead` concept. - On a Title slide, a Markdown image supplies the subject visual and an ordinary paragraph supplies the subtitle or presenter line. - A sequence of Markdown image paragraphs is rendered as a two-row gallery. Alt text supplies each caption; a following ordinary source-credit paragraph retains the attribution. The Prologue keeps its 18 images in two rows of nine and its declared 17 caption steps.

rules.name: Content region and whitespace
rules.body: On content slides, reserve a content region covering at least 40 % of the slide area, spanning at least 85 % of its width, and extending to y ≈ 800 or below. These measurements describe the available layout region, not the bounding box of visible letters. Short content may leave purposeful whitespace. Do not stretch bullet spacing or push text toward the outer edges to satisfy a visible-ink target. Image-and-bullets compositions reserve at least 60 %; Title, Section, Quotation, and Image slides are exempt.
